regions.text: 以上において定言的、假説、離接の三地平にあつて偶然性の闌明を計つた。

quote.translation: In the foregoing I have sought to elucidate contingency on three horizons, the categorical, the hypothetical and the disjunctive.

regions.text: 定言的偶然は、定営到断において、概念としての主語に對して遠語が非本質微表を意味するときに成立した。すなはち、或る言明的判断が主語と逮語との同一性を鋏くために確證性従つて必然性をもたないことが明かになつた場合である。

quote.translation: Categorical contingency arose when, in a categorical judgement, the predicate signifies a non-essential mark in relation to the subject taken as concept; it is the case, that is, in which it has become clear that an assertoric judgement, lacking the identity of subject and predicate, has no apodicticity and consequently no necessity.

regions.text: 假說的偶然は、假説的判断の理由蹄結の嬲係以外に立つものこして成立した。すなはち、理由と蹄結との同一性によつて規定せられたる確證性、従つて必然性の範國外にあるものとして成立した。

quote.translation: Hypothetical contingency arose as what stands outside the relation of ground and consequent in the hypothetical judgement, which is to say as what lies outside the range of the apodicticity, and so of the necessity, determined by the identity of ground and consequent.

regions.text: 離接的偶然は興へられた定言約到斷もしくは假説的刻断を離接的到断の一盛分肢と見て他にもなほ教個か

quote.translation: Disjunctive contingency, we may say, arises when we regard a given categorical or hypothetical judgement as one member of the division in a disjunctive judgement, and think that besides it there exist several other members.
